headline: AMD separates agent execution from inference in an open rack blueprint

source.title: Introducing AMD Helion, Agentic AI Compute at Rack Scale

read_evidence.scope: Complete original AMD October 12 release, reference OCP design, configurable cooling, EPYC-only versus EPYC+Instinct MI350P racks, token routing, partner comments, actual planned November availability and forward-looking caveats.

reading_time_evidence.caveat: Editorial approximation, not measured reader session

summary: AMD introduced Helion, a proposed rack design for agent workloads, not a shipping product. A CPU-only configuration targets execution work with up to 32,768 EPYC cores, while an integrated enterprise design combines EPYC processors and MI350P accelerators. An integrated token router directs model calls, and partner availability is planned for November.
why_it_matters: Agent deployments mix orchestration, tool execution and model inference. Engineers can estimate each workload separately, check rack power and networking constraints, and challenge the vendor's planned availability before treating Helion as production capacity.
related_coverage: See companion October 14 coverage for infrastructure design, work context, task review and safe skills.
image_alt_intent: Detailed cutaway of two Helion rack configurations: high-density EPYC CPU execution on left, hybrid EPYC plus MI350P inference on right, separated by token-routing fabric and annotated power, cooling and interoperability boundaries.
